newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore bank announces high first half profits.
newsitem.headline: Singapore bank announces high first half profits.

text.p: Singapore's Overseas Union Bank Ltd (OUB) announced much better than expected first half net profits on Friday and said earnings in the second six months of the year should be even better.
The bank said net profits in the six months to June 30, 1997 rose 27.2 percent to Singapore $180.85. Consensus analyst forecasts were for a rise of some 20 percent to around S$170 million.
"Clearly the numbers show we have done very well," OUB president Peter Seah told a news conference.
"We believe this is a good story. This performance was achieved on the back of a 22.4 percent rise in loan portfolio for the group."
Seah said second half results should be even better.
"I don't do crystal ball gazing, but I expect in terms of absolute quantum our second half numbers to be higher than in the first half," he said.
Seah said he had been asked at the full-year results news conference in March whether the company's net profit for the full year 1997 would reach Singapore $360 million.
"I said, maybe," he said. "I think I have met that expectation."
If the second half matches the first six months, the full-year net would be S$361.7 million.

Seah said the results were helped by strong contributions from outside Singapore, which accounted for around 35 percent of profits. The biggest part of that came from Malaysia, which accounted for 16 percent of profits.
Seah said the bank was "quite comfortable with our current exposure in Thailand", bailed out by a $16 billion rescue package put together, mainly by Asian nations, in Tokyo on Monday.
